ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle BAC=70^\circ$. The triangle $\triangle ABC$ is rotated $70^\circ$ clockwise around point A, with the corresponding points of B and C after rotation being B' and C', respectively. Connecting BB', what is the degree measure of $\angle BB'C'$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Given the properties of rotation, we know that: $AB=AB'$, $\angle BAB'=70^\circ$, and $\angle ACB=\angle AC'B'=90^\circ$ \\
$\therefore \angle ABB'=\angle AB'B=\frac{1}{2}\times (180^\circ-70^\circ)=55^\circ$ \\
In $\triangle AB'C'$, $\angle AB'C'=90^\circ-\angle B'AB=20^\circ$ \\
$\because \angle BB'C+\angle AB'C'=\angle AB'B$ \\
$\therefore \angle BB'C'=\angle AB'B-\angle AB'C'=55^\circ-20^\circ=\boxed{35^\circ}$

Read the diagram as a rotated right triangle with C' on the original line AB and the target angle between B'B and the vertical-looking side B'C'. Choose coordinates with A at the origin and the original ray AB as the positive x-axis; set AB = 1. From the text, ∠BAC = 70° and ∠C = 90°, so AC is the adjacent leg to angle A and AC = cos70°. A 70° clockwise rotation sends B = (1,0) to B' = (cos70°, -sin70°), and sends C to C' = (cos70°, 0), which matches the diagram where C' lies on AB. Then vectors from B' are B'B = (1 - cos70°, sin70°) and B'C' = (0, sin70°). Therefore the desired angle from B'C' to B'B has tangent (horizontal component)/(vertical component) = (1 - cos70°)/sin70° = tan35° by the half-angle identity. Hence ∠BB'C' = 35°.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle BAC=70^\circ$. The triangle $\triangle ABC$ is rotated $70^\circ$ clockwise around point A, with the corresponding points of B and C after rotation being B' and C', respectively. Connecting BB', what is the degree measure of $\angle BB'C'$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:}

Given the properties of rotation, we know that: $AB=AB'$, $\angle BAB'=70^\circ$, and $\angle ACB=\angle AC'B'=90^\circ$ \\
$\therefore \angle ABB'=\angle AB'B=\frac{1}{2}\times (180^\circ-70^\circ)=55^\circ$ \\
In $\triangle AB'C'$, $\angle AB'C'=90^\circ-\angle B'AB=20^\circ$ \\
$\because \angle BB'C+\angle AB'C'=\angle AB'B$ \\
$\therefore \angle BB'C'=\angle AB'B-\angle AB'C'=55^\circ-20^\circ=\boxed{35^\circ}$
